episodes.211430: A strong cold front resulted in a brief but widespread period of gale-force winds during the early to mid-morning hours across the Chesapeake Bay (north of Smith Point VA) and the tidal Potomac River.
episodes.211895: The combination of multiple rounds of rainfall over the previous few days and heavy rain across portions of the Ozarks lead to additional flooding.
episodes.212520: There was extensive river flooding along the Wisconsin River, Fox River, and Rock River in southern Wisconsin in April. The river levels were above normal after 5 inches of rain fell over the 5 days, and then another episode of heavy rain of 3 to 5 inches occurred on April 17th. In addition, vegetation was still fairly dormant so the grass was not able to soak up much of the rainfall.
episodes.212591: A cold front moved across the Mid-Atlantic on April 19. Winds became gusty behind the front across the Chesapeake Bay, York River, and Virginia Coastal Waters.
episodes.213007: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front and one of these storms produced large hail.
